Good morning class. Welcome to our first class. Today, I will provide the framework for how we will learn this semester. What are we learning? How are we learning? Why are we learning?

This is a class of ideas, so it's crucial for you to pay attention and understand how these ideas connect with each other. If I'm not clear, ask me a question. In fact, make it a habit to ask as many questions as possible because that way you will learn more. Learning will be more fun for you and clearer.

So, let's get in the habit of asking questions. Wherever I am confusing, wherever I'm speaking too fast, or wherever you don't understand, interrupt me. 

First, we will discuss Emmanuel Kant this semester because he is the greatest philosopher in Western history. He teaches us how the world works and tells us that we can never know objective reality. There is a reality called noumena that is not knowable to us; it's a world we can never access because we perceive the world through our senses.

Our senses warp the world, changing it into a structure we can process called phenomena. Time and space are examples of this: they do not exist outside of us but are necessary for us to understand reality. The world works by us perceiving nomena and turning it into phenomena for processing. In other words, reality is what we imagine it to be.

This semester, I want to train you to augment your imagination so that you see the world more clearly. This class is not about what to think; it's about how to think. Let me explain the structure of the course: we will analyze the past, present, and future in order to construct a more objective reality for ourselves. We will fail but the process of trying will train our minds to think more critically.

In the present, we will study geopolitics—why there is war in Ukraine or the Middle East. We will try to understand why this is happening by formulating an analytical model and using it to make predictions about the future. These predictions will tell us if our model is correct.

Why do we do this? Because these predictions will help us determine if our model is accurate, similar to testing an artificial intelligence system against reality. By doing this, we aim to create an ethical model that makes correct predictions and then use it to analyze the past to reveal the secret history of humanity.

You may not know this, but the history you learn in school or believe you know is false. It's a system implanted into your brains by powerful people. This semester, we are looking at how power works because if we can figure this out, you will achieve liberation and freedom—understanding how others manipulate you and empowering you to live the way you want to live and see the world that is true to you.
